name: code_read_file

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/notifications/templates.ts

Password reset (and other) email links are built from BASE_URL, which falls back to `http://localhost:3000` whenever the `PUBLIC_URL` environment variable isn't set in the deployment environment. That's why the reset link resolves to localhost for users after the last release. Fix by ensuring `PUBLIC_URL` is set to the production URL in the deploy config, and/or failing loudly at startup if it's missing in production instead of silently defaulting to localhost.

input.title: Fix password reset emails linking to localhost in production
input.body:
File: src/notifications/templates.ts

BASE_URL falls back to "http://localhost:3000" whenever process.env.PUBLIC_URL is not set, and this fallback is used for password reset links, rollup report links, and scheduled export links. If PUBLIC_URL isn't configured in the production environment (e.g. after last week's release), reset emails end up pointing users to localhost instead of the real site.

Proposed fix: stop silently defaulting to localhost in environments where it isn't appropriate. Either require PUBLIC_URL to be set (throwing or failing fast at startup if it's missing in non-development environments) or derive BASE_URL from a validated config value (e.g. config.publicUrl) that is guaranteed to be set correctly per environment, rather than reading process.env directly with a localhost fallback. This ensures password reset, rollup, and export links always use the correct public URL.
